concept.name: Commitments of Traders report
concept.definition: A weekly report published by the CFTC providing a breakdown of each Tuesday's open interest for markets in which 20 or more traders hold positions at or above CFTC-established reporting levels. The legacy report separates open interest into commercial, non-commercial, and non-reportable holdings; disaggregated and TFF variants provide finer categories.
concept.intuition: It is a weekly census of who is long and who is short in each major futures market — hedgers versus speculators versus small traders.
concept.mechanics: Compiled from confidential daily large-trader data collected under the CFTC's market surveillance program, published Fridays reflecting Tuesday positions. Available in futures-only and futures-and-options-combined formats, short and long formats; long-format reports add nonreportable positions, crop-year breakdowns, and concentration ratios for the largest four and eight traders.
concept.failure_modes: The data are three days stale at publication and classify traders, not trades — a 'commercial' position is not necessarily a hedge, and staff classification involves judgment. Categories can be reclassified over time, and historical disaggregated data were backcast using recent classifications, reducing accuracy further back in time.
concept.misconceptions: COT is not a real-time positioning feed, and 'noncommercial net position' is not 'the dumb money' — the category includes sophisticated macro funds. Extreme readings are not mechanical contrarian signals; large speculative positions can persist and grow for months in trending markets.
concept.example: The legacy COT for corn shows commercials net short 300,000 contracts and noncommercials net long 220,000; analysts track how these net positions shift week to week as a positioning indicator.
